messages:
taylor: heads-up: found another redaction ordering footgun in the node/python quickstarts when dev reloads are enabled. Debug logs sometimes print raw request ids before our redaction runs.

mike: ugh that sounds familiar. minimal repro?

taylor: clone github.com/redwood/sample-apps/node-telemetry, set LOG_LEVEL=debug, start with nodemon --watch. Trigger POST /auth. snippet: 
```
[DEBUG] nodemon: spawn child pid=4321 reqid=tmp-101
[DEBUG] http: parsed headers - reqid=tmp-101
[INFO] app.handler: login.success - reqid=REDACTED
```
When LOG_LEVEL=info it looks fine.

priya: same pattern we've seen: dev reload handlers (nodemon/uvicorn) add their own log handlers or emit debug before our SDK attaches the redaction filter. In reload mode child processes inherit different handler order.

mike: is telemetry.init() called in main or in an app startup event?

taylor: in quickstart it's called in index.js after some requires. Moving init to the very top fixes it locally. But in reload mode nodemon sometimes emits logs in the parent/child that don't pass through our filter.

priya: for mitigation we should: 1) update quickstarts to call telemetry.init() synchronously at the top of main, 2) add a small SDK helper register_known_server_loggers() that adds our redaction filter to common loggers (nodemon, uvicorn.access, gunicorn.access, pm2). The helper should be idempotent and safe to call multiple times.

mike: +1. Also add a short onboarding doc note warning about --reload/dev modes and recommending the helper or disabling auto-reload for verifying redaction.

priya: I prototyped register_known_server_loggers() in node SDK; it iterates known logger names and attaches filter if logger.getHandlers exists. For Python I'll add a helper that attaches a logging.Filter to uvicorn.access and gunicorn.access.

taylor: sweet. can we add a CI smoke test to quickstarts? start the dev server programmatically with LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG, send a request with a fake token, and assert logs don't contain the token/reqid. Retry startup to reduce flakiness.

mike: yes add that. keep tests lightweight and skip on CI flags if flaky.

docs-bot: Drafted docs change: docs/telemetry/dev-reload-caveats.md - "Why dev reload modes can bypass redaction and how to mitigate".

telemetry-bot: Created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/1832 — "Dev quickstarts: reload/dev servers can emit logs before redaction filter attaches; add SDK helper + quickstart fixes". Labels: devex, telemetry, bug.

priya: I'll open PRs for node and python quickstarts with the helper and a README note about init order. I'll include the CI smoke test and link the issue. ping here for reviews.

mike: thanks all — we should also add a short note in the Dedicated onboarding checklist to verify sidecar/startup ordering.

taylor: added, will try to reproduce in a dedicated staging pool later today and update the issue with results. :thumbsup:
